title: Cross-Sectional Area of a Folded Gutter
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A long metal sheet $16$ inches wide has its two edges turned up by $x$ inches to form an open gutter with a flat bottom. Express the gutter's cross-sectional area $A(x)$ and the permissible values of $x$.

steps.title: Decompose the Folded Profile
steps.explanation: Each turned-up edge steals $x$ inches from the flat bottom, leaving a bottom of width $16-2x$ and two walls of height $x$.
steps.why: Conservation of the sheet's width determines the bottom dimension.

steps.title: Compute the Trapezoid-Free Rectangle Area
steps.explanation: With vertical walls the cross-section is a rectangle: height $x$ times bottom width $16-2x$, i.e. $A(x)=16x-2x^{2}$.
steps.why: The carrying capacity of the gutter is proportional to this cross-sectional area.

steps.title: Restrict x to Physical Values
steps.explanation: Folds of zero height carry nothing, and once $x$ reaches $8$ the two folds exhaust the whole sheet, so $x$ must lie strictly between $0$ and $8$.
steps.why: Both geometric parts must remain positive for a real gutter.
